title_guess: How bank lending creates liquid money and inflation, NDTL, and RBI's levers on lending: SLR and CRR, rates on RBI loans to banks (bank rate, LTRO, repo, MSF) and the reverse repo
recurring_cast: shield: a 'Monetary Policy' shield reading 'Supply of Liquid Money' with a CONTROL band, held up by arms rising from the RBI coin; parked in a left side panel for the whole video as a context rail
brand_logo: the RBI emblem coin (inside the shield, later at the top of the loan tree)
bank_building with a 'Loan' arrow to a person: the spine of the board from 72 s to the end
vault: green deposit panel with two safes, open with cash (demand or savings deposits) and closed (time or fixed deposits), later titled NDTL
tick_mark: green tick meaning 'counts as liquid money', later tagged as the bank's asset
percentage_badge: red % signs on the SLR and CRR arrows and on each rate
Less/More fork under the Loan arrow with a condition under each branch, used three times
running_examples: no numbers anywhere in the video; one running money path instead: your fixed-deposit money goes to the bank, out as a loan to someone who spends it, demand rises, prices rise
the same Less/More fork for each lever: SLR and CRR % up means less lending; RBI's rates up means fewer loans; reverse repo up means banks park more with RBI and lend less

best_moments.why: fixed-deposit money flows down to a bank and out as a Loan to a person, and the green 'liquid' tick lands on the loan: money that was not liquid becomes liquid by being lent
the borrower turns into a dancing figure throwing notes: purchasing power and demand made visible without text
a Less/More fork hangs under the Loan arrow with the condition written under each branch: the lever and its effect on one line; the same fork returns for interest rates and for reverse repo
after four rate names, the whole rate tree is wiped and replaced by one dotted line from RBI to the % on the bank's loan: 'all these rates are one lever on lending rates'
for reverse repo the loan arrow turns round (bank up to RBI); later 'More Loan' marks that arrow and 'Less Loan' the arrow to the person: the direction of money carries the idea
the monetary policy shield stays in a side panel for the whole video, so every lever is seen against the frame 'RBI controls the supply of liquid money'

weak_moments.why: NDTL as a liability (customers' money that must be returned) is speech only; nothing shows money owed back to depositors
bank rate, LTRO, repo and MSF appear as red labels 5-13 s before they are named and are then set aside as 'covered in other videos': a label list, not a mechanism
liquid money is defined by a sentence banner that appears about 28 s before the matching words are spoken; the speech in between is partly missing from the transcript
the reason banks park money at a higher reverse repo is a grey paragraph box
no numbers at all: no CRR or SLR values, no rates, no deposit amount, so no lever is ever run with a worked example; the arrows read '% of NTDL' (typo for NDTL)

facts to check before reuse: reverse repo shown as RBI's tool for absorbing bank money, though since April 2022 the Standing Deposit Facility is the floor rate; NDTL is simplified to demand plus time deposits; SLR is said to be only government securities

segments.teaches: recall of the previous video: RBI uses monetary policy to control the supply of liquid money, which drives purchasing power, demand and inflation, and so price stability and growth

segments.idea: RBI's monetary policy controls the supply of liquid money, and that supply drives demand and inflation

segments.teaches: liquid money is money that can be turned into cash at any time without restriction or penalty: cash and demand or savings deposits are liquid; fixed (time) deposits are not, because early withdrawal brings penalties

segments.idea: money you can turn into cash any time without penalty (cash, savings and demand deposits) is liquid money; a fixed deposit is not
segments.shown_as: a person holds cash marked with a green tick, notes fluttering from the hand; two arrows lead from the person into a panel with an open safe full of cash (demand or savings deposits) and a closed safe (time or fixed deposits); the open safe gets a green tick as it is called liquid money, the closed safe never does
segments.example: your money as cash, in a savings account, or in a fixed deposit

segments.teaches: when a bank lends fixed-deposit money to a person or company, money that was not liquid becomes liquid; more liquid money raises purchasing power, demand and the general price level, so bank lending raises inflation

segments.idea: a bank loan turns locked-up deposit money into spendable money, and more spending pushes prices up
segments.shown_as: the closed fixed-deposit safe sends an arrow down to a bank, the bank sends a 'Loan' arrow to a person, and the green 'liquid' tick lands on the loan; then the plain borrower turns into a dancing figure throwing notes as purchasing power and demand are named
segments.example: your fixed-deposit money lent by the bank to another person or company

segments.teaches: how much a bank can lend depends on its NDTL (net demand and time liabilities: its demand and time deposits); deposits are liabilities because they are customers' money, loans are assets because they earn interest, so banks want to lend as much as possible, which raises inflation

elements.what: banner and cash holder cleared; the deposit panel moves up above the bank
NDTL over the deposit panel
'Net Demand & Time Liabilities'
'Assets' with a small arrow to the green tick on the Loan line

segments.notes: 4 change events. NDTL title about 1.5 s before 'NDTL' is spoken; the full form lands on its words (131 s). 'Assets' appears about 2.6 s after 'asset'. Liability (141-150 s), the bank's motive and the problem it creates (158.8-171.5 s) are speech only. NDTL is simplified to demand plus time deposits.
segments.idea: a bank's deposits (NDTL) are what it owes and set how much it can lend; its loans earn interest and are its assets
segments.shown_as: the board is tidied to deposit panel, bank, loan, person; the deposit panel is titled NDTL with its full form beside it, and an 'Assets' tag points at the ticked Loan as loans are called assets

segments.teaches: SLR (a share of NDTL kept in government securities) and CRR (a share of NDTL kept with RBI, earning no interest) are mandatory and set by RBI; raising them leaves banks less to lend and controls inflation, lowering them does the opposite

red arrows marked '% of NTDL' from the bank into each safe

the Loan line forks into Less and More

segments.idea: RBI makes banks set aside part of their deposits (SLR, CRR); a bigger share leaves less to lend, a smaller one more
segments.shown_as: two safes, SLR and CRR, appear beside the bank; a red '% of NDTL' arrow runs from the bank into each; dotted lines from the RBI coin reach both; then the Loan line forks into Less and More, labelled 'if SLR and CRR % is more' and 'if it is less'

segments.teaches: banks can also borrow from RBI (the banker of banks), long term or short term, and RBI charges a different rate on each kind: bank rate or LTRO for long term, repo or MSF for short term

segments.idea: banks can borrow from RBI for the long or short term, and RBI sets the rate on each kind of loan

segments.teaches: RBI sets these rates; if it raises them, banks raise their lending rates, fewer people borrow and inflation falls; if it lowers them, more people borrow

segments.idea: higher RBI rates mean dearer bank loans, fewer borrowers and lower inflation; lower rates the reverse
segments.shown_as: a yellow band ties the two rate signs together and a dotted arrow carries it down to a % on the bank's loan line; the loan line forks into Less and More with 'people will take more loans' and 'fewer loans' under them; then the whole tree is wiped and one dotted line runs straight from RBI to the loan %

segments.teaches: RBI can also borrow short term from banks; the rate it pays is the reverse repo rate, set by RBI; raising it makes banks park surplus funds with RBI, so they have less to lend

segments.idea: RBI can borrow banks' spare money at the reverse repo rate; raising that rate pulls money into RBI and leaves banks less to lend
